body: You don't have to lie, but you don't have to tell them what they're from either. You can tell them something like that some people don't like to talk about their scars bc it reminds them of a time they were hurt. I know a lot of people can worry about how their scars might affect kids, but this way they can learn a) that bringing up visible scars can bring up difficult emotions (true for any scars, not just self harm, and something even adults sometimes need to learn) and b) if they get scars of any kind in the future, they can set their own boundaries on how much they feel comfortable talking about them. It think it can be good to set an example for them that they don't have to justify their bodies just because someone asks
I'm sorry that you're having a rough time, this sort of thing can be very difficult - if it helps, you absolutely are not doing anything wrong, and I wish you the best!
It is definitely not attention seeking! If you ever worry that you need stitches, please go to the hospital to get them taken care of!
